name: Harrow homestead
detail: Intervale house on the river flats north of New Haven village. Kitchen, boot room, south-facing door.

name: South-block orchard
detail: The block that took the 1927 silt. Stake iron still in the third row.

name: Harrow sugarhouse
detail: A cupola sugarhouse at the edge of the maples, ledger nailed above the arch.

name: Homestead cistern
detail: Stone cistern between house and orchard. Flood silt under the frost ring.

name: New Haven Mills flat
detail: Hamlet flat where the water has a memory of the old mill seats.

name: Marble Works race
detail: The old marble-mill buildings and the race that still argues with Otter Creek.

name: County survey room
detail: A rented room off Court Street. Not a throne. A table, a cabinet, the flood book.

name: Below the falls
detail: The creek under the village falls, where marble dust and ice go when they are done being useful.

name: Saturday exchange yard
detail: The yard behind the feed store where scion wood and rumors change hands. No counter quest. A conversation in mud.

name: Lower gate at the pulp mill
detail: Millrace by the covered bridge. Ansel's wheel. The pin is on the left hand side of the gate.

name: Hill barns
detail: Two barns on the hill road when the town road is shut with mud or ice.

name: Neighbor fence to the Morgan farm
detail: A private fence line in the horse country. Not the college farm's office. Cora Belden's paddock.

name: Falls basin
detail: Otter Creek at the Vergennes falls. Slick rock, coat-catching eddies, the Rouleau count.

name: Rouleau night kitchen
detail: A kitchen on South Water Street that feeds the falls crew when the wage meeting runs long.

name: March meadow
detail: Downstream of the Vergennes works. Henry March's cows. The place the extra water goes.

name: Chimney Point landing
detail: Vermont landing of the Lake Champlain Bridge. The log is kept on this shore only.

name: Vermont abutment
detail: The Vermont abutment of the 1929 bridge, and later the place where the new span meets the same ground.

name: Lamb's Creemee
detail: A pullout stand on Route 17 that lives on bridge traffic and a book of orders.

name: Larabee's Point
detail: Ferry landing. A bell that is rung for the dead who are not in the water anymore.

name: The overhang cut
detail: A limestone cut above Bristol. The Marble Vein is in this stone as a fact of work and of unrealized names.

name: Powder shack
detail: Off the cut. The key is ordinary. The use is not.

name: Quarry supper hall
detail: Long tables, limestone in the cuffs, grace said by whoever Elena appoints.

name: Notch slide
detail: A mud and rock slide on the Lincoln gap approach. School-bus road and quarry lane diverge here.

name: Pellegrin porch
detail: Kin porch east of the cut, where envelopes go when the shack is closed.

name: Dead Creek log
detail: A sunning log in the Dead Creek marshes. Queen's place.

name: Pike barn
detail: Earl Pike's barn at the marsh edge. Hay, stake, dog hair, no museum.

name: The wrong pond
detail: A farm pond Queen can be walked to. She does not prefer it.

name: The Quiet Household
detail: Waite house. Plates, a stopped clock, an east room that is not for guests.

name: East room
detail: The bed made for the life that did not continue.

name: Whiting line fence
detail: The surveyed line between Whiting and Orwell where it crosses Abbott ground.

name: Abbott plot
detail: A family plot that the line would move into Orwell if the fair copy wins.

name: Keene loft
detail: Above the Cornwall grange. Choir, stove, sack of unsent letters.

name: Post corner
detail: Walter Keene's counter. The rule about the dead is taped to the wood.

name: Notch turn
detail: A pull-off on the Ripton road where the wind takes a card out of a hand. Not a campus.

name: Route 7 pullout bench
detail: A memorial bench the state calls a right-of-way problem.

name: Burnham garden
detail: Ten feet of garden that a kind survey gave to the wrong woman.

name: Gray corner post
detail: A post one foot inside Alma Gray's dooryard. Goshen does not have many witnesses.

name: Outlet shed
detail: A shed at the Lake Dunmore outlet used as a dry-store for copies when Middlebury basements flood.

name: Landing road
detail: The road down toward the lake where unlogged crossings get talked about after church.

name: Ridge box
detail: A newspaper box on Monkton Ridge where Pearl leaves a flavor card when the stand is boarded.

name: Spare line
detail: An old blazed line in Hancock used once, in the oath year, as a place to practice refusing.

name: Granville bed
detail: The empty road through Granville. A place the choir does not sing. Used only as a wrong destination someone proposes and Ellis refuses.
